title: GPARAM layer stack and priorities
summary: Lighting, fog, post and sky values come from GPARAM files stacked in priority layers. Later layers override earlier ones key by key, where the key is (bank, row). A bank number is ((area+100)*100+block)*10000.
values: Exe priorities: default 1, templates 2, MDLVW 3, MapBase 4, block layers 5 to 9, MapOverride 10, remo / dying / eclipse 11 and up. Record defaults come from the (0,1) or (1,0) template. Ceremony rows pick the sub id (gparamId) of the file.
how: Draw param loader merges files by priority, then the per-frame blend applies the ids chosen by the collision part and events.

ours.where: src/map_lights.rs; src/grading.rs (reads one gparam set per arena)

check: Dump the layer list for m11_00 and check that the MapOverride (10) value wins over MapBase (4) for the same key.
note: Whether remo/dying layers sit at fixed priorities above 11 comes from the exe only.

needs.why: ceremony picks the gparam sub id

title: Light set, fog and envmap chosen by the standing collision
summary: Each collision part stores four ids at MSB +0x70: LightSetID, FogParamID, LightScatteringID, EnvMapID. The part under the player picks the lighting for the whole scene, using the same sticky collision that chooses the visible map.
values: gparam config = [LightSetID, FogParamID, LightScatteringID, EnvMapID]. Collisions carry light set rows 100 / 110 / 120 / 130 and map pieces row 0. SetHitCollision copies the draw params from the part.
how: ChrIns::SetHitCollision 0x1409f5820 copies the part's draw param block; frames then blend toward the new ids.
check: Walk from the Castle roof into the interior: the light set row changes with the collision.
note: The exact link from a map piece's own draw params (row 0) to the collision rows 100 to 130 is open.

needs.why: ids are keys in the stack

title: LightSet record fields
summary: A light set holds four directional light slots, hemisphere ambient colours, shadow settings and sky colour terms. Colours are stored as rgb with a separate intensity W and are uploaded squared.
values: Light and hemisphere colours upload as rgb*rgb*W. Four light slots; only slot 0 gets the sun-shadow factor.
how: Per-frame light constants buffer, then the deferred directional pass.
check: Print one LightSet row and compare slot 0 colour times W with the lit result of a white surface.

title: Time of day variants of a map's lighting
summary: A map's lighting comes in variants for a time of day: environment variants 0 to 5 map to hours 0, 6, 12, 18, 22 and 2. Events and a clock flag choose the variant, so the same place can show dusk or night.
values: Story clock flags 9800 to 9803 set by common event 820 (clock) and event 100 (sky and envmap selection). Variants 0 to 5 = 0 h, 6 h, 12 h, 18 h, 22 h, 2 h.
how: EMEVD events pick a Gparam Sub ID and envmap; blending is the draw param fade.
check: Set flag 9801 and compare the Outskirts sky colour.
note: The meaning of flags 9800 to 9803 is read from event structure, not from a recording.

title: Story state lighting (burning Castle, fights)
summary: Event instructions set the area lighting and gparam sub id for story states. The burning Castle, the castle boss fights and the late game fires use their own sub ids.
values: Set Area Gparam Sub ID 2003[88] (43 uses), Set Lighting 2003[81] (42 uses), Set Area Envmap 2003[80]. Castle fight sub ids 0740 and 0750 (sub 40 and 50). Set Ceremony 12 uses (m15 and m25).
how: EMEVD layer: the event sets a map's sub id, the draw param loader loads that variant.
check: Load m11_01 with flag 8302 set and check which sub id is used.
note: Gating of the burning state by flag 8302 is an open-question.

title: Scene light units to engine units
summary: The game's lights are in a scene unit. To show them in Bevy a constant is applied that makes the pre-exposure agree.
values: SCENE_TO_BEVY = pi / exposure = 3135.61.
how: Fixed multiplier in the light upload.
check: Compare a grey card under the sun in game and in the clone.
note: Scenes read 2 to 5 times retail brightness, cause unresolved.

title: Unexplained brightness of the sun in row 100
summary: The sun in light-set row 100 reads about 4.4 times row 0, and sekiro-rs scenes end up 2 to 5 times brighter than retail frames. The reason is not found.
values: Ratio 4.4 (row 100 over row 0).
how: Possibly a missing factor in the deferred light pass or the auto-exposure target.
check: Compare an in-game and clone screenshot of a white wall at noon.

title: Point light falloff
summary: Native point lights in the lit pass use a window falloff, a wrap term on N.L and a quadratic fade. The result is a soft light that wraps a little around surfaces.
values: fall = saturate(1 - d^2/R^2); t = 1.4/(1.4 + d*b); wrap = t^2 + (1 - t^2)*N.L; diffuse = Diff*fall*wrap/(1 + 0.7*(d*b)^2).
how: Deferred local light pass from the disassembled shader.
check: Place a light by a wall and read the brightness profile.

title: BTL map point and spot lights
summary: BTL files hold the placed local lights of a map (lamps, fire, windows). Colours and radii are converted at load, and the map offset is applied before the X mirror.
values: Outskirts map offset (90, 3, -40) with a 20 degree Y rotation is applied to BTL coordinates.
how: Light list per block sent to the local light pass.
check: Walk to a lantern and see a warm local pool of light.

title: Sun shadow factor
summary: Only light slot 0 (the sun) casts the shadow; the shadow factor from the cascaded map multiplies its contribution. The other slots are unshadowed.
values: Four light slots, shadow factor on slot 0 only.
how: Shadow pass then the deferred light combine.

ours.where: Bevy cascaded shadows with the arena sun

check: Stand in a doorway: sun on the floor cuts at the shadow edge, torch light does not.

title: Volumetric froxel fog
summary: Fog is computed in a camera frustum grid (froxels) with geometric depth slices, using the FogParam rows picked by the light set. It scales by GameScale and includes a height term and a fixed density option.
values: Terms: GameScale, HeightFogOffset, FixedDensity; EnableAnalyticalFog defaults to false.
how: A compute pass fills froxel scattering, the lit pass reads it.
check: Look across a valley: far objects fade into the fog colour.

title: Height fog profile
summary: The height term uses an exponential profile above the fog height and a mirrored curve below it, so density goes smoothly through the fog plane.
values: profile(q) = exp(-q) for q >= 0, else 2 - exp(q).
how: Evaluated per froxel in the fog pass.
check: Fly through a valley fog layer and check there is no jump at the plane.

title: Fog colour encoding
summary: Fog colours are stored as bytes, quantised, then raised to the power 2.2 and scaled by W, so the editor value is a gamma-space colour.
values: colour = pow(byte/255, 2.2) * W.
how: Loader converts GPARAM fog entries.
check: Compare a fog colour sample in a still with the converted value.

title: Sky dome choice
summary: The m89 library map holds the sky domes. Common event 100 chooses a group (8907000 to 8907070) from the story clock and area state, and activates it.
how: EMEVD 2012[1] activates the map part group; the dome follows the camera.
check: Change the story clock and watch the dome swap at dusk.

title: SkyDome_Ver2 shader
summary: The sky material has a switch selecting layers and packs colours like HDR colours: rgb^2.2 times Intensity (GXMaterialParam_HDRColor).
values: Switch 0 or 1; colour = pow(rgb,2.2) * Intensity.
how: Decoded material and shader code.
check: Render a dome material with and without the 2.2 pow: the sun disc is wrong without it.

title: GIIV irradiance volumes
summary: Global illumination uses BC7 3D irradiance volumes (GIIV), one for each Env_Box, giving diffuse ambient per spot. Boxes blend by priority and fade distance.
how: Env_Box parts in the MSB point to the volume textures; sampled in the lit pass.
check: Walk from a lit courtyard into a shaded eave: ambient colour changes smoothly.

title: GILM reflection probes
summary: Each Env_Box also has a 128 by 128 BC6H cube map (GILM) for specular reflection.
values: 128^2 BC6H cubes, one per Env_Box.
how: Cube sampled by reflection vector in the lit pass.
check: Look at a metal surface: the reflection shows the local environment.

title: Env box blending
summary: Overlapping Env_Boxes blend by priority; a box fades in over a border so lighting does not pop at the edges.
values: Priority and fade fields on the Env_Box region.
how: Evaluated in the lit pass.
check: Cross a box border and look for a seam.

title: Tone mapping (mode 7 Sensitometric)
summary: The final colour is tone mapped with a film-like curve built from two exponentials, mixed by a constant.
how: Post chain pass before grading and LUT.
check: Render a grey ramp and fit the curve.

title: Auto exposure and adaption
summary: Exposure is 2^Exposure. MiddleGray is a log2 target, and the adaption moves exposure toward it with soft Min and Max limits.
values: Exposure scale 2^E; MiddleGray in log2; adaption soft limits Min/Max.
how: Luminance average, then eye adaption each frame.
check: Step from a dark cave into sun: the screen starts bright and settles.

title: Bloom
summary: Bloom blurs bright parts with a 7 tap Gaussian across a few levels and adds them back.
values: gain = Alpha*Luminance / sum(Smooth^i); 7 taps.
how: Post chain after exposure, before tone mapping.
check: Look at the sun disc glow.

title: LUT and colour matrix
summary: The grade uses a 16 by 256 strip LUT (layout x = r, y = 16*b + g) and a colour matrix applied in hue, saturation, value, contrast order. Vignette is a field that neither project implements.
values: Strip size 16x256; matrix order hue/sat/value/contrast.
how: Final grading pass with GPARAM post records.
check: Toggle the LUT and compare skin colour.

title: Layered map material shaders (M[Multiple])
summary: Map materials blend two or three texture layers with a mask, in M[Multiple] and M[MultipleGround] shaders. Static switch variants (GXFT_SATStaticSwitch) pick which layer features compile.
values: Materials: M[Multiple], M[MultipleGround]; sat switch variants.
how: Material parameter blocks read from the FLVER material and the MTD.
check: Look at ground blends of mud and grass.

title: Emissive and lamp shaders
summary: Lamps, fire bowls and glowing props use emissive material shaders with an HDR colour and intensity.
values: Emission colour rgb^2.2 times intensity.
how: Same HDR colour packing as the sky.
check: Look at a lantern: the glass glows over the lit scene.

title: Character shaders (DetailBlend and Fresnel)
summary: Characters use a skin and cloth shader with detail blend and Fresnel rim terms from the material.
values: Params from the MTD of c-prefixed models.
how: Forward lit with the same lights.
check: Check Wolf's rim light in the Castle.

title: FXR effect format and player
summary: Particle effects are FXR files: a tree of emitters and appearance actions. The player runs them with soft particles, distortion, tracers and lights.
values: Appearance actions 603, 604, 606, 607, 608, 609 and 10012.
how: FXR files from the sfxbnd; ours is a clean-room player, sekiro-rs adds more fields.
check: Spawn a sparks effect on a deflect.

title: FXR colour handling (disagreement)
summary: Two readings of the effect colour path exist. Our kb keeps the sqrt 3 factor in hue_squared because A/B tests against clips match. Sekiro-rs removed it because the disassembly shows no such factor.
values: sqrt 3 in hue_squared (ours) versus none (sekiro-rs). Also contested: the sign of node X rotation, and emitter direction 6.
how: FXR colour shader.
check: Render the same effect in both and compare to a clip.
note: Keep both readings until the exe settles it.

title: Effect lights (action 609)
summary: Action 609 creates a light bound to the effect. Its colour is squared when the light is built.
values: Colour squared (builder 3892e0).
how: FXR light builder.
check: Fire a spark effect in a dark room: the walls light up.

title: Placed map effects
summary: Maps place SFX with MSB regions (type 5 SFX, type 6 wind SFX) and with events. ModelSfxParam maps a model plus a relative id to an effect id, covering torches, smoke and idol glows.
values: ModelSfxParam row = model*1000 + relative id; 312 placements in Outskirts and 287 in Castle.
how: Map loader spawns effects from regions; EMEVD 2006[1,2,3] spawn and delete them.
check: Stand near an Outskirts torch and see the fire effect.

title: Cloth simulation
summary: Wolf's scarf, banners and hair use Havok cloth on the character skeleton. It is pinned at the root and reacts to gravity, wind and simple collision capsules.
values: Havok cloth data in the cloth binder; gravity and wind from the engine.
how: Per frame solver after animation.
check: Run in a circle: the scarf trails behind.
note: Ours uses its own approximate solver.

title: Blood and decals
summary: Hits stain the world: a decal id is built from the hit material and the attack power. HitEffectSfx tables give the effect and HitEffectSfxAngleParam chooses by angle.
values: DecalParam hit-stain id = 600000000 + materialSfx1*1000 + decalBaseId + atkPow.
how: Hit effect system after damage.
check: Kill a basic enemy: a blood decal appears on the ground.

title: Water surface shader
summary: The water surface is a special material with flow, reflection and refraction. Neither project has it. Ours draws a dark translucent plane.
how: Gap in both projects.
check: Look at a pond: ripples are missing.
note: Gap. Description of the target look is from play, not data.

title: Grass and foliage rendering
summary: Grass blades are batched patches using GrassLodRangeParam distances for LOD and shadows.
values: 9 rows; row 0 LOD0 40 m, LOD1 120 m, LOD2 160 m, shadow 1000 m.
how: Grass sidecar from the map export.
check: Step back from a grass field and watch the blades thin out.

title: Mesh LOD display
summary: Distance LOD for map pieces uses LodParam rows with a crossfade. Characters use their own LOD.
values: Row 0: 30 / 60 m, crossfade 0.2 s.
how: See map.lod-bank-selection.
check: Walk away from a building and watch the roof detail drop.
